own_solution.law: For an infinite square well, E_n = n²(hc)²/[8(mc²)L²]. Thus the emitted photon has energy E_4 - E_1 = 15(hc)²/[8(mc²)L²], and wavelength λ = 8(mc²)L²/(15hc). At L = 0.5 nm, the energy gap is 22.5675 eV and λ = 54.9462 nm.
assumptions: Use the nonrelativistic infinite-well spectrum; the relevant energies are much smaller than the electron rest energy.
The stated quantum numbers identify the levels at the time of emission.
The photon energy equals the level spacing, with negligible recoil of the confining apparatus.
The separately defined dot does not alter the specified well potential.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T425C and T6BE7 replace the explicit widening increment of 2.4 nm with an unspecified 'small amount', violating the required same-number-and-unit condition for variants.

notes: The base physics is well posed at the supplied precision. Widening the well before emission gives L = 2.9 nm and increases the wavelength by (2.9/0.5)² = 33.64. Widening it after emission has no causal path to the emitted wavelength, so this is D rather than cancellation. Changing the separately defined dot is also D in the stated model. All four numerical increments agree at 2.4 nm; the two qualitative increments prevent the complete sentence family from satisfying the explicit variant requirement. No unspecified increment is needed to calculate either qualitative sentence's target answer.
